notes: Both coders agreed on the document stance for both documents (syllabus guidance = delegates; D08.0 = restrict). Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs course-start/before-course/during-work for rationale and principle sentences; resolved by using general for rationales and principles addressed to students, during-work for sentences about submitted work, and before-course for policy-design steps like co-creating expectations. (2) Actor on rationale lines (student vs all): student when the passage addresses 'you', all when it is a preface or premise. One blanket-ban warning went to UNCOVERED. (4) Modality: should vs may for optional advice, informs vs must for procedural statements. The automatic aligner paired four units wrongly (adjacent but different list items); I re-paired by hand, which also changed matched counts. Unmatched: A-only 5 (all kept); B-only 10, of which 7 kept and 3 dropped (the 'rule of thumb treat it as human' lead-in, which the two kept sub-rules restate; 'the following policy applies to this course', a lead-in with no rule; and a resource-list link title).
